news.title: What would a 64-team World Cup look like?
news.lede: Infantino has opened the door to another World Cup expansion, with Fifa vice president Alejandro Dominguez in favour of it as early as the 2030 edition - but what would a 64-team tournament actually look like? From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground.

news.title: Gianni Infantino's top aide's damning statement in full after QUITTING over 'irresponsible' World Cup sale plot
news.lede: A SENIOR adviser to Fifa chief Gianni Infantino has released a damning statement after resigning in protest over their World Cup sell-off plan. Former US Soccer president and Goldman Sachs vice-chair Carlos Cordeiro suddenly stepped down from his role as an aide to the controversial executive on Friday. The move came in response to Fifa’s proposal to create a subsidiary company called the Fifa Forward Enterprise, which would oversee the World Cup. Private investors would then be able to purchase stakes in the company, essentially taking ownership of a chunk of the World Cup.

news.title: UEFA to boycott World Cup if Infantino sell-off plan goes ahead
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. England, its fellow UEFA nations and CONCACAF have unanimously voted to boycott the upcoming men’s and women’s World Cups if Gianni Infantino goes ahead with plans to sell off shares in the tournament to private investors. UEFA’s 55 member nations held a virtual crisis meeting on Thursday to discuss Infantino’s recently announced plans to privatise and sell shares in the World Cup.

news.title: Fifa chiefs criticise media for 'misreporting' World Cup sell-off plans
news.lede: Executives at world football's governing body Fifa on Friday said "incorrect" media reports had "disrupted" the presentation of its proposals to open up the World Cup to outside investors. Fifa wants to create a €17 billion subsidiary, Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE), and give a 20 percent stake in the operation to external investors. European football's ruling organisation Uefa has led the protests against the proposal, accusing Fifa of putting the sport up for sale. On Thursday, Uefa's 55 member nations voted unanimously to boycott all Fifa tournaments – including the World Cup – if Fifa continues to promote its plans.

news.title: Ranking World Cup performances by Bayern Munich players
news.lede: From 1982 to 2022, every single FIFA World Cup Final featured at least one Bayern Munich player. That streak came to an end in 2026, as France lost to Spain and England lost to Argentina in the semifinals. However, that doesn’t mean that Bayern didn’t have plenty of representation in the World Cup. Today, we’re taking a look at Bayern Munich’s World Cup performances from worst to best (Nathaniel Brown and Ismael Saibari are not included as they only joined Bayern midway through the tournament).

news.title: Uefa could boycott the World Cup if Fifa plan goes ahead – what happens next?
news.lede: The 55 member countries of Uefa – Europe’s governing body for football, whose teams are among the world’s best and tend to dominate international competitions, have drawn a line in the sand. On July 30, Uefa pledged to boycott all competitions run by Fifa, the sport’s global body, if a proposal to package up and sell interests in the World Cup to private investors went ahead. A few hours later, Concacaf, the North American football confederation, also rejected the proposal. But how did it get to this?

news.title: FIFA advisor quits, calls World Cup stake sale 'bad deal for football'
news.lede: Carlos Cordeiro, a senior advisor to FIFA president Gianni Infantino, has resigned in protest over a controversial proposal to sell a stake in the World Cup, labelling the plan 'a bad deal for football' and raising concerns about the organisation's financial strategy. Carlos Cordeiro, senior advisor to FIFA president Gianni Infantino, resigned with immediate effect on Friday in protest at proposals to sell a stake in the World Cup, calling the plan "a bad deal for football". Cordeiro, a former banker and ex-US Soccer Federation vice president hand-picked to help grow world soccer for FIFA, announced his immediate resignation, saying he could not "stand by while FIFA considers selling a stake in the World Cup".
